title: In Vitro Germination of Austropuccinia psidii Urediniospores
author: Alyssa M Martino

steps.title: Harvest spores from infected leaves
steps.instruction: Shake heavily infected leaves into a paper bag to collect fresh urediniospores.

steps.title: Dry spores in desiccator
steps.instruction: Transfer the collected spores to an uncovered glass Petri dish, place the dish in a desiccator containing silica gel beads, and dry for 24–48 h.

steps.title: Sieve spores to remove debris
steps.instruction: Pass the dried spores through a sieve to eliminate plant material and dirt.

steps.title: Aliquot and store spores
steps.instruction: Dispense spores into Nunc CryoTubes (or similar containers) for short‑term or long‑term storage; for long‑term, freeze at –80 °C or in liquid nitrogen, noting that this may lower germination rates. Use spores immediately after desiccation when possible.

steps.title: Prepare inoculum suspension
steps.instruction: In a 15 mL centrifuge tube, suspend spores in sterile distilled water to a concentration of ~1 mg mL⁻¹, adding Tween 20 to a final concentration of 0.05 % (5 µL mL⁻¹). Mix gently by inverting several times; verify concentration with a haemocytometer if desired.

steps.title: Rehydrate inoculum
steps.instruction: Incubate the spore suspension for 30 min to allow rehydration before use.

steps.title: Apply inoculum droplets to agar
steps.instruction: Pipette 2 µL of the inoculum onto the surface of an agar plate, placing distinct 2 µL droplets to cover the plate, then seal the plate with parafilm.

steps.title: Incubate plates for germination
steps.instruction: Place the sealed plates in an incubator set to 18 °C, 75 % relative humidity, in the dark for at least 8 h.

steps.title: Assess spore germination
steps.instruction: Under a dissecting microscope, count germinated spores in each droplet; consider a spore germinated if its germ tube is at least twice the length of the urediniospore. Expect 70–80 % germination with fresh spores.
